utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-17-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Bralo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, counsel. My name is Mark Harmon. Appearing with me is Mr. Fergal Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, my name is Jonathan Cooper, counsel for Mr. Bralo, and I appear with Virginia Lindsay who is legal consultant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bralo, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's why I asked you this question. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Well, good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. This is a hearing in accordance with Rule 47, 50 and 62 ter of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This Trial Chamber is seized with the filing of documents relating to Rule 62 ter filed by the Prosecution dated 19th July, 2005. There are three documents attached to this motion, which are the plea agreement, proposed amended indictment and the factual basis. Since we just received this document this morning, I would like to have the parties to brief us very briefly on the contents of those documents. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would be glad to do so. The three documents that the Trial Chamber has received consist of a proposed amended indictment, a proposed plea agreement and a factual basis to support a plea agreement. That's the nature of the three documents. If you want additional details, I can give Your Honours additional details in respect of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me start with the proposed amended indictment. The proposed amended indictment is a streamlined indictment from the previous indictment. The previous indictment had 21 counts. This indictment is a streamlined version of the previous indictment. It has eight counts. The new indictment consists of a new count, a count of persecutions, which is count 1, of the proposed amended indictment, and there is a second new count, that count is unlawful confinement which is found in count 6. The streamlining of the indictment consists, for example, of the previous indictment in counts 1 and 2 has been streamlined in the new indictment. You'll find that in count 7 the amendment and the proposed amendment from the old indictment to the new indictment consists of essentially withdrawing the old count 2, a violation of the laws or customs of war, for the same conduct. In the previous indictment, Your Honours will see under counts 3 and 4, cruel and -- inhumane and cruel treatment, and the new indictment has only one of the charges, the original charges, from the previous indictment, and that's found now in count 8. Counts 5 through 8 of the old indictment, which was -- which were multiple charges relating to a set of murders that took place between the 21st of April and the 10th of May, 1993, those counts have been streamlined. We essentially withdrew three of those counts, and now that conduct, which was found in counts 5 through 8 of the old indictment, is now found in count 2 of the new indictment. Yes, that's correct. And the counts relating to counts 9 through 21, rape and torture, now are reflected in the new indictment in counts 3 through 6. And we, as I say, have added one additional count in respect of that conduct, unlawful confinement. So what we are presenting in terms of the indictment reflects in the new indictment the conduct, much of the conduct, I should say, from the old indictment, plus the addition of a persecutions count. The persecutions count, count 1, relates to conduct that relates to the attack on the village of Ahmici that occurred on the 16th of April, 1993. So that is what the amended indictment is, in terms of what we are proposing, and we ask leave of the court to accept the amendments. The plea agreement document is a document that sets forth, for the Court's benefit, the terms of the agreement in terms of reflecting this is a knowing and intelligent waiver of rights. It outlines the nature of the offences and there is a section that deal with penalty and sentencing. I should say, in terms of this agreement, this is an unconditional plea. There are no promises or inducements made by the Prosecutor's office in respect of securing the pleas that Mr. Bralo intends to tender to this Court. Finally, Your Honours, in support of the proposed -- of the pleas, we have submitted for Your Honours a factual basis. These are facts that are agreed upon by both the Prosecution and the Defence and form the basis on which the Court can rely in respect of each of the charges. So those are the three documents that we have submitted in the package that we filed this morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any observations from the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The Judges may ask some questions to the parties. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have also been provided with some supporting material, that is, two witness statements. Do they play any role at this moment in --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The only role they play, Your Honour, is to support the proposed amendments, to establish that there is a prima facie case to support the amendments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that attached to both the supporting documents, I do not know whether there are any protective measures but I think we can deal with it without even referring to the names of the witnesses who gave those statements, I see quite a number of documents attached, one of them some six or seven, the other one apart from a sketch which is clearly explained in the statement, also a similar document as attached to the other one, of which I'm not aware, as a matter of fact, what it actually is. Are these certificates of birth or are these certificates of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were attached some death certificates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Death certificates, yes. Then I take it since they are all similar and they indicate names, that these are death certificates of the victims of -- because the names correspond with the names on the annexes to the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, they are death certificates for some of the victims, not all of the victims. And, yes, they are the certificates for some of the names in Schedule A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check that. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Harmon, in your statement, you said that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it's unconditional plea agreement. Would you please elaborate on that point? What do you mean by unconditional?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I will be glad to, Your Honour. Unconditional means that this agreement is not conditioned upon Mr. Bralo doing anything or providing anything to the Prosecutor's office. He is accepting the pleas. There have been -- the charges on their face. He is -- has not been promised anything by the Prosecutor's office nor has he been induced to plea by any recommendation, for example, of a sentence range or sentence itself. There are absolutely no promises made to Mr. Bralo, and the issue of how this case ultimately is resolved will be through evidence that will be adduced at a later hearing, should the Court accept the guilty pleas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cooper, do you have any observations on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are indeed unconditional pleas. They are entered freely and entirely voluntarily. The information which underlies each of the counts was either information that was known already to the Prosecutor and was included in the original indictment, or was information which came new to the Prosecutor from this defendant himself, and in relation to all the counts, those in the original indictment and if Your Honours are so minded, in the amended indictment, the defendant enters pleas entirely unconditionally, and they reflect his concern and desire to express his remorse without condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Orie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, having looked at what I now know are death certificates, may I draw your attention to the death certificate which concerns Adis Salkic? On Schedule A you give as the date of birth the 20th of December, 1978, whereas the death certificate seems to indicate a date of birth different. Might be a typo but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might be a typo. But without a copy of the death certificate here, I'm not in a position to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one is the 20th, the other is the 28th. It might be a typo, but I just note it's not really consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is noted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultations among the Judges, this Trial Chamber carefully examined each of the counts in the amended indictment and any supporting materials the Prosecution provided. This Trial Chamber is in the position now to find out that a case existing against the accused. So the newly amended indictment is confirmed by this Trial Chamber. It is so decided. Well, since the indictment is confirmed, we believe that we should ask the accused, Mr. Bralo, to re-enter his plea to all those counts. Mr. Bralo, did you have an opportunity to discuss the contents of the amended indictment with your counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you understand --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you understand the meaning of each count?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to remind you that you have the right to have the newly amended indictment read out, or you could waive this right. Which way do you prefer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waive the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Therefore, my suggestion is that I read out each count in the newly amended indictment. You may plead guilty or not guilty, as the case may be. Are you ready to plead at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's begin. How do you plead to count 1: Persecution as a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm guilty and I honestly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 2: Murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm guilty, and I very much regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. Count 3: Torture or inhumane treatment as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions as punishable under Article 2(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. Count 4: Torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 5: Outrages upon personal dignity, including rape, as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 6: Unlawful confinement as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Article 2(g) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 7: Unlawful confinement of civilians as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Article 2(g) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 8: Inhumane treatment as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Article 2(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, and I truly regret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. The Trial Chamber records pleas of guilty of eight counts by the accused. Mr. Bralo, since you pleaded guilty to eight counts in the newly amended indictment, the Trial Chamber would like to find out from you whether you understand the details of the plea agreement you entered into with the Prosecution. Do you understand my question, Mr. Bralo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have received a plea agreement between you and the Prosecution. I just want to know whether you have had an opportunity to read the contents of this plea agreement. Did you sign that plea agreement? And did you discuss it with your counsel about the contents of this plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm informed of everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I also would like to know whether you have entered guilty plea voluntarily and out of your free will, whether you were threatened or coerced in any way to make this plea.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your counsel have an opportunity to advise you of the consequences of pleading guilty to eight counts in the newly amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This Trial Chamber would also like to find out from you, when entering into this plea agreement, you understand that the Trial Chamber is not bound to accept the range of sentence agreed by yourself and the Prosecution, if there is any in the future. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage -- you may sit down, please, Mr. Bralo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, I believe that the Bench will withdraw to deliberate whether we are going to accept the guilty plea as well as the plea agreement. We will break for 15 minutes, and we will resume at quarter to 4.00. --- Break taken at 3.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe this Bench is in the position to make the ruling. The Trial Chamber has considered the particulars of the facts in the plea agreement and is satisfied that they do form sufficient factual basis for finding that the accused is guilty on those counts and therefore makes a finding of guilty and enters the conviction of eight counts against the accused, Mr. Bralo. The Trial Chamber will issue orders relating further proceedings in due course. At the same time, as for the Schedule A, there is a mistake, in our view, concerning the date of the birth. I hope that the party could be -- address it at this moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It appears to be a typo -- a typographical error and the death certificate controls so we will -- if Your Honours wish, we can make that change orally or we can submit a new Schedule A with the correct date for that particular individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could just leave out the date. I think the month will be quite enough, and the oral submission is sufficient. There is no need to fly papers everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the Trial Chamber will now move to the next stage, about the possible date for hearing on the sentencing, and we would like to find out from both parties how they intend to make their submissions on the sentencing issue. Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will be making, at this point in time, written submissions, and if there is an evidentiary hearing, we hope but I can't say for certain to be having viva voce testimony as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. How about the specific date?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Any date that's convenient for the Trial Chamber is convenient for me. I can tell Your Honours with one exception, on the 25th of September, I will be occupied. We are to start the Krajisnik case, as I recall, either on the 5th or the 12th of September, and in that first two-week period of the recommencement of the Krajisnik trial, I suspect I will be fully engaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And how about the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to the form of the submissions, we intend to file written submissions. There are inquiries that are necessary in the course of the next four to six weeks but we anticipate being in a position to file a written submission by -- certainly by the second week in September, if that's convenient to the Court, and then to be in a position to proceed with a sentence hearing, I would suggest, if convenient with the Court, in the second or third week of October. That would give us sufficient time to conduct the inquiries we need and to present the submissions that we need to in a form which is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are you in a position to inform us about whether you would like to call any witnesses concerning of the mitigating aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Forgive me, Your Honour, that's a matter that we need to consider. I don't anticipate any great number or any great length of evidence, and if that's of assistance, then I'm glad. But the question of calling evidence is a matter that we need to review carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope you could inform us in your final briefs on this aspect. Maybe you have to file some 65 ter documents. Well, so tentatively, could we set on the 16th of September as the date for the parties to submit their written briefs? And if there is any sentence hearings, we will set it on the 10th of October. Of course, this is subject to the further notice in the future. I see both parties are nodding. And are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Cooper?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Thank you. And nor for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bralo, do you have anything to say at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Well, I believe that's all for this hearing. So the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.53 p.m.
